newsitem.title: INDIA: India's Congress says wants stable government.
newsitem.headline: India's Congress says wants stable government.

text.p: India's Congress party, which provides crucial support to the ruling United Front coalition, said on Friday it wants a stable government and has a sweet relationship with the coalition.

Newly elected Congress president Sitaram Kesri told a news conference the party was committed to a stable relationship with the United Front until Congress had a chance to form a new government after fresh general elections.
Asked about the United Front, Kesri said: "Our relations are sweet and will remain sweet. And when the mandate of the country is for a coalition, we will obey it."
"It is wrong to interpret that we will withdraw our support to the government. That will continue for a good number of days," Kesri said.

Congress in March withdrew its vital backing to then prime minister H.D. Deve Gowda's government and later helped to topple him in a parliamentary confidence vote. It resumed support to the coalition only after it agreed to replace Deve Gowda.

"We withdrew support on March 30 due to certain occurrences," Kesri said without elaborating. "Their behaviour is now better than it was earlier. Therefore, Congress wants to continue its support, and the United Front should also see that it takes care of Congress interests."
